title: Light That Illuminates All
subtitle: It burns so bright that its radiance evaporates everything—including your ego.

content.text: I saw doubt on Mademoiselle Brume's face. As a diviner, you encounter that look more often than people think.
Some have called me a schemer, a fraud, as the Vigiles Bureau did. Perhaps they are watching me even now, listening in to our very conversation.
Some were frightened by what I could see but kept coming back to sate their own curiosity.
Some showed nothing but disdain—not for me, but for the very idea of a predetermined future. I admired their courage.
Brume was not any of these. She was a fourth kind—one who tries to ignore the prophecy but, in doing so, only finds herself carried further into its stream.

branch.text: Oops. Have I let it slip?
Well, I suppose there is no use pretending now. There was a disagreement about my decision to take a certain handful of arcane objects without consulting their rightful owners.
In the end, I paid all their penalties, among other not-so-charming consequences.
Not that it has done anything to prevent them from hounding me at every turn. To them, it seems I am only a fear-mongering schemer who knows secrets best left unknown.
Someone who walks between eras and through the "Storms," what is your view on fate?
Few people can imagine the nature of your position. No more than three, I would wager. And I wish I could say I was one of them.
Alas, I am but a puppet dangling at the end of fate's thread. My limited vision cages my imagination.
Though I may still see a little more than most people, I cannot do as I was meant to.
Your hands are tied—is that what you're saying?
I have lived long enough to know better than to act against fate.
Though, in fact, what I would have done differs very little from what I was meant to do.
What do you think? Is it perhaps fate that determined my personality, or my personality determining my fate?

items.text: Rue de la Paix, Paris
A dizzying crowd has filled Place Vendôme, flowing in from every direction.
The young driver leans against her car door, kicking at a small stone while watching the passersby.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: "Tomorrow ..." She never said the time. She's not planning to keep me waiting until the evening, is she?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Or has she already gone in?
She turns her head. The ornate carved door of the Parlor of Crystals is shut and shuttered, just as it was a few hours ago.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Should I knock again? Someone must be in at this hour.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Hello?
This time, the door opens the very moment she knocks.
But once it does, all she can see is the dim corridor ahead.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ah, finally. Perhaps they didn't hear me knocking before?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Er, hello? Right, I suppose I'll just let myself in.
She steps inside. But the very instant her foot touches the floor, the last trace of light vanishes.
The tiny dragon's flame barely lights the way, its tail swishing weakly.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: They could at least leave a light on for the customers.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Hello? Anyone here? I think my "friend" arrived before me. She's about this tall—just enough to always be looking down her nose at you?
Adèle reaches out along the wall, feeling her way forward from memory.

items.speaker: Feufeu
items.text: Grrrh!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What is it, Feufeu?
Following the dragon's upward gaze, she spots a few faint, translucent figures with pointed ears.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Sprites. Of course. Where else would they be, if not in a diviner's parlor?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Let me be clear. I don't care what kind of mischief you're up to in here. Just don't let it involve me!
The sprites shriek, batting at the harmless flames licking their bodies. Even if they can't be burned, the fright is real enough.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Heh. Not so funny when the joke's on you, huh?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Now, lead on. Bring me to the owner of this place, understood?
Ignoring what sounds like their tiny frustrated protests, she follows the sprites to a door. Each one of them slipping inside ahead of her through the glowing crack.
She pushes it wide open.
Parlor of Crystals
The room looks as if it were woven from a million scattered threads of light.
The thought crosses Adèle's mind as she takes in the transparent, shimmering crystals around her, their reflections gilding the dust in the air.
Here, every breath she takes seems to take in some of the shimmering light, almost like she is devouring the very spirit of the crystals.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: How pretty.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Never seen a parlor quite like this. The way these crystals are displayed ... It feels like they're not meant for sale or for exhibition.
She breathes as softly and shallowly as she can, attempting to blend into the light.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Is it the lighting that's giving them such an otherworldly glow? Or maybe ...
Perhaps you are thinking of the Sephirot. When captured, they may be manifested through crystals.
A voice echoes from afar—bright, clear, like the sound of gentle tapping on a glass pane.
Some believe it is through these Sephirot that the creator formed our world. Without them, the divinity is incomplete.
The ten Sephirot ... The astral light, the flames of the fire which burned in the bush, the glowing stream which flows from the Tree of Life, the "numerals," "spheres," "enos"—
—and all aspects of reality.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ah, then you must be ...

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Madame Beryl Bouanich?
The shop's owner smiles and nods. No further explanation is needed. Anyone who's seen her would know exactly who she is.
She extends her hand, brushing a softly glowing pendulum with her fingertips.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Through certain objects and rituals—or by gnosis gifted at birth—we may catch a glimpse of a splendor that is not of this world.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: These crystals are one such object. In their reflection, we are shown the hidden secrets of the Archive of Imagery.
Her voice soothes Adèle's nerves, though it comes out so softly that she struggles to register the meaning.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Madame, did you ...

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I am pleased that you have made your way here, Madame Tavernier. That door was left open just for you.
Sitting Room, Parlor of Crystals
Her teacup exudes the calming floral scents of Darjeeling, and with each bite of Madeleine cake, her remaining tension melts along with the buttery richness.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: So I'm the first one here. I see.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: And you were at Madame Raymond's salon the other day to retrieve your crystals?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Indeed I was. I have been occupied in business overseas and neglected the security of this parlor.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Someone has been taking my defective crystals and pawning them off to other diviners.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Few are able to detect their flaws. But, minute as they are, they render them hazardous for ritual use. I must act before any further harm is done.
She looks toward Adèle, her expression softer still, sweeter still, despite her words of caution.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: For that, I owe you my thanks, Madame Tavernier.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You showed courage that day, in your words and actions.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Just Adèle will do. And there's really no need to thank me.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Truth be told, I probably wouldn't have interfered if the diviner hadn't tried to make a fool of me.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Ah. Those words still bother you, do they not?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: No, not at all. I don't take things like that seriously, you know.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: After all, fate—it's just a matter of belief, isn't it?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You do not believe, yet you cannot seem to put it out of mind. Is that so?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Hah. Please, madame. You aren't about to start with the prophecies like all the others, are you?
She raises her cup again and reclines against the chair.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Forgive me. It's not that I think all diviners are liars. It's just that it's hard to believe that fate is shaped by any kind of higher power. It seems just as likely to me that most divinations are simply self-fulfilling prophecies.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: And whether they be from a higher power or a crystal ball, I won't let prophecies dictate my life.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: If I have a fate—some road I'm destined to travel—then I will first go as far as I can down every other road until it's the only option I have left.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: There's still so much I want to do!
But the woman only laughs, not with mocking laughter but with something like genuine delight at her words.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Fate, dear, is a universal law—the cause and effect of all events. Just as the path of light through a crystal may be predicted to find its refraction, one road inevitably leads to another.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: While some believe our paths to be unpredictable, others see them as written from beginning to end.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: But there is little use in searching for "meaning" in such a thing as fate.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: My reading foresaw your coming today, and here you are. The light passes through the crystal and falls as it must, as it ever was to be.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You knew I'd come? Then, what about my friend?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I saw only you.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Damn! She didn't even bother to come! What is she thinking?
Adèle mumbles in confusion, but Beryl has already moved along to the next question.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You came here only to find your friend?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I, well, yes, you could say that.
Beryl's eyes track away, gazing out distant and unfocused, as if she wasn't aware of the person in front of her at all.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: There is something more—a question, not about the truth of fate, but of how you might act upon it.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: The curse in your family, or as some may call it, the path of the Tavernier.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You wonder whether it is your time to walk it, do you not?

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: The call must be answered! Walk with the wise, but beware their words. Beware the gaping abyss of death.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: What lies below shall reflect what lies above—one shall ascend, but all must be paid.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: All must return! All must restore—

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: How come every diviner I meet these days seems to know about that curse?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Is obscure jewel lore really so popular in this city?
Adèle says it like a joke. That's how she always treats the subject.
Mockery felt better to her than fear.
Beryl only nods in reply.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Madame Raymond foresaw the future, but she peeked too far, and for that, paid dearly.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You mean ...
She still doesn't want to hear that kind of answer.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: No, no, no. Please tell me you're just teasing me.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You're saying that it wasn't her fear of the Beasts of Gévaudan that killed her but what she saw in my future?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Please, Adèle. Allow me to finish.
Beryl shakes her head. Somehow just that gesture alone is enough to lift her heart.
—Only for her next words to put it right back into a vise grip.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: The fate she saw was not entirely yours. There is a shadow which lingers on you.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: In a way, it is true. You are indeed cursed.
